entry.evidence: there are few researches to investigate the geothermal potentiality

steps.action: The authors cite prior Curie point depth and heat flux estimates from aeromagnetic spectra over the northern Western Desert (Saada 2016) and Egypt-wide maps (Elbarbary et al. 2018).
steps.quote: Saada (38) utilized airborne magnetic measurements to investigate the Curie point depth (CPD) and heat flux at the Northern section of the Western Desert

steps.action: The authors pose the aim: examine the subsurface structure of the AGB and its relevance to geothermal resources using potential-field data validated by well temperatures.
steps.quote: The purpose of current research is to examine the subsurface structure of AGB and its relevance to the presence of geothermal energy resources

steps.action: From the cited structural framework, the authors state a working expectation that the basin's faults and structures can host geothermal resources.
steps.quote: We might state that there is a complicated situation with various structures in and around AGB that can accommodate several geothermal resources.

steps.action: The authors compile existing data: a GETECH Bouguer gravity grid (10 km, 600 m altitude), a GETECH TMI grid (1000 m), and bottom-hole temperatures from 138 oil and gas wells (2000-4800 m).
steps.quote: GETECH also provided the airborne magnetic measurements in the shape of a consolidated 1000 m grid of total magnetic intensity (TMI)

steps.action: The authors design the validation: BHT-derived temperature gradients will be used to verify the CPD-derived outputs (flowchart, Fig. 4).
steps.quote: The results from BHT data were used for verifying the outputs of CPD.

steps.action: The authors correct BHTs with the Waples et al. (2004) empirical formula, compute gradients with Ts = 26.7 °C and heat flow with conductivity 1.8-2.6 W/m °C, and map 0.022-0.034 °C/m and 43-84 mW/m2.
steps.quote: Geothermal gradients vary from 0.022 °C/m to 0.034 °C/m, with an average of 0.03 °C/m

steps.action: The authors reduce the TMI grid to the pole, compute radially averaged spectra in 48 overlapping 87 × 113 km windows, apply the centroid method (Zb = 2Z0 − Zt), and map CPD at 17-21 km.
steps.quote: The map of CPDs for the AGB was mapped using a minimal curvature interpolation for Zb, with a range of 17 to 21 km

steps.action: The authors convert CPD to gradients assuming 580 °C at Zb, and to heat flow with k = 2.0 W/mK and no radiogenic source, giving 0.026-0.034 °C/m and 52-67 mW/m2, which they compare with continental crust values (Brott et al.).
steps.quote: the calculated heat flux rates range from 52 to 67 mW/m2 and an average of nearby 60 mW/m2

steps.action: The authors invert the Bouguer gravity with GRABLOX for a two-layer model (2.2 and 2.67 g/cm3, Occam regularization, 2nd-order polynomial regional), report an RMS misfit of 0.007, and map basement depth at 4.5-7 km.
steps.quote: The conducted model has a Root Mean Square (RMS) value of 0.007.

steps.action: The authors compare the inverted sediment thickness with well data along a profile crossing well GPAA-3 (Fig. 11), noting that no well reaches basement.
steps.quote: A high correlation exists between the depth of the expected basement depending on a 3D gravity inversion and well data.

steps.action: The authors compare the AGB CPD range with Tanaka et al.'s (1999) tectonic classes and conclude that the basin's thermal conditions resemble stable continents despite its unstable-shelf setting.
steps.quote: with deeper CPDs (20 km to 30 km) found in stable continental areas and plateaus

steps.action: The authors regress BHT-measured gradients against CPD-derived gradients (44 points, R² = 0.90; Figure 13, p. 4515) as cross-validation with independent well data.
steps.quote: The geothermal gradient from CPDs and those from BHT are highly correlated, with roughly 90% agreement (Fig. 13).

steps.action: The authors classify the average gradient and heat flow against known resource types as indicating low-temperature hydrothermal resources, and link this to hydrocarbon maturation.
steps.quote: [...] gradient of 30 °C/km and a heat flow of around 60 mW/m2 indicate the existence of low-temperature hydrothermal resources

steps.action: The authors plot basement depth and CPD along an E-W profile across the AGB (Figure 14, p. 4516) and compare uplifts of basement with rises of the Curie surface.
steps.quote: Shallow CPD and uplifts in the Precambrian basement rocks were found to have a link

steps.action: The authors set aside radiogenic heat production in the sedimentary cover as a contributor to the heat flow.
steps.quote: the sedimentary cover is might be free of any radioactive sources

steps.action: The authors keep the shallower-CPD areas (eastern, NW trends and central AGB) as promising regions for geothermal exploration.
steps.quote: may appear the promising regions of geothermal exploration

steps.action: The authors keep the claim that basement rocks are primarily responsible for the basin's geothermal potential, citing the coincidence of shallow CPD, basement uplift and high heat flow.
steps.quote: suggesting that basement rocks are primarily responsible for geothermal potentiality on the AGB

end.claim: Shallow Curie depths, basement uplifts and high heat flow coincide in the AGB, suggesting that basement rocks are primarily responsible for the basin's geothermal potential.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the spectral-analysis estimate of Curie point depths and the gradients derived from them, there would be neither the cross-validation with BHT nor the basement-CPD link behind the claim.

gates.evidence: All data were existing GETECH grids and industry BHT logs, not acquired under a hypothesis (§3 ¶1-2). The CPD-derived gradients could have failed to match the BHT gradients (§6 ¶2, Fig. 13), but the causal claim about basement control was never tested against a stated rival. Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Curie point: ferromagnetic to paramagnetic transition as the base of magnetic sources
Radially averaged power spectrum analysis of gridded fields (centroid method)
Occam's principle regularized inversion minimizing roughness and misfit
Bottom-hole temperature logs from EGPC, BP and GUPCO wells

limits: No 'first' or 'previously unknown' statement; the paper only notes few prior geothermal studies of the AGB (§1 ¶2). The abstract's ranges (CPD 17-22 km, gradient 25-34 °C/km, heat flow 52-86 mW/m2) differ from the body's (CPD 17-21 km, gradient 0.022-0.034 or 0.026-0.034 °C/m, heat flow 43-84 or 52-67 mW/m2), and these are not reconciled. The conclusion's 'shallower CPDs of > 19 km' is internally odd. The BHT-derived and CPD-derived heat flows differ (averages 72 vs 60 mW/m2), which goes undiscussed. Figure 13 (p. 4515) uses 44 data points out of 138 wells; how points were selected and how wells were matched to CPD windows is not stated. Calling R² = 0.90 '90% agreement' is the authors' reading. No uncertainties are given for CPD, gradients, heat flow or basement depth. There is no sensitivity test on window size (87 × 113 km), on the 580 °C Curie temperature, on conductivity (1.8-2.6 vs 2.0 W/mK) or on the density contrast, and no time-since-circulation values for the BHT correction are reported. The basement check rests on one well (GPAA-3) that does not reach basement (§5 ¶4), so the 'high correlation' is unquantified. The heat-flow calculation assumes no radioactive source (§4.2 ¶4), and the conclusion that the sedimentary cover may be free of radioactive sources (§6 ¶4) reuses that assumption; this is inference by the coder (circular). Figure 14b (p. 4516) annotates a local basement subsidence undetectable at the Curie surface, which the text does not discuss. The prior CPD maps (Saada 2016; Elbarbary et al. 2018) are cited but not compared quantitatively. The fault-controlled expectation of §2 ¶3 is never tested. The paper cites 'Demerdash et al.' for basin boundaries, but the referenced work is an electrical-machines paper (reference list, p. 4519), apparently a citation error. Sub-claims: the CPD, gradient, heat-flow and basement-depth maps are estimate_with_resolution in form, but without stated uncertainty; the low-temperature hydrothermal resource class and the 'stable-continent-like' conditions are best_explanation. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded; the paper was revised (received February 2022, revised October 2022) but the changes are unknown. Composition none_fits: this is a mapping and estimation study cross-validated with independent well data, with no rivals, no set conditions and no repeated natural events fitted as a regularity.
